review_defects.where: apps/Model Plane/rust/services/model-gateway/src/grpc.rs:1857 (list_mcp_tools -> forwarded_capability_bearer -> runtime_registries::mcp_tool_listing -> hydrate_mcp_registry, runtime_registries.rs:361-423 and replace_org at :201)
review_defects.scenario: list_mcp_tools now passes the raw x-capability-authorization header into hydrate_mcp_registry without verifying it. Every other hydrate caller (http_routes.rs mcp_list/mcp_share) takes a VerifiedCapabilityBearer. hydrate_mcp_registry runs reg.replace_org(org, empty) and ownership.replace_org_kind(org, empty) BEFORE its HTTP request, and also drops the org's discovery catalog. Two ways to hit it: (a) any caller allowed on ListMcpTools sends `x-capability-authorization: Bearer junk` (a user identity passes authorize_rpc plus authorize_user; the header only has to be a plain Bearer). capability-core answers 401, hydrate returns Err after the clear, and the org's MCP servers and ownership sidecar stay empty on that replica. Every proxy_mcp_tool for the org (inline chat and Do runs) then returns `mcp server not found` until some verified HTTP path rehydrates. (b) Without an attacker, every governed Do-run offer forwards a bearer, so every segment start clears and refills the org cache and forces re-discovery of every server. A concurrent proxy_mcp_tool from another run in the same org that lands in the window, or between reg.replace_org and ownership.replace_org_kind, fails not_found. The failure is not transient, so it is not retried.
review_defects.fix: Verify the forwarded bearer before using it, as the HTTP routes do (the VerifiedCapabilityBearer path, with the same org pin), or accept it only from a service identity. Make hydration fetch first and swap the org's registry, ownership and catalog only on success, never clear before the request. Consider hydrating only on a cache miss or after a TTL, not on every governed listing.

review_defects.where: apps/Model Plane/rust/services/execution-core/src/runtime_loop/mod.rs:1219-1240 (execute_governed_mcp) with permission/mod.rs RunGate::view / run_view; views are written only at offer time in agent.rs merged_tool_defs_governed
review_defects.scenario: The read-mode check (mode.allows(view.class())), the plan-mode and leaf checks and the autonomy rung all read the ToolClassView captured when the segment's offer was built. The signed per-call decision is never compared with it. Example: the offer at segment start sees mcp__srv__x declared `read`, approved, digest D. Before the model first calls it, the registry tightens the row to `external_write`; the digest is unchanged and review_state stays approved, which Decide() leaves as allow at floor none. On the first call, capability_policy.pin_binding pins the NEW class (it is the first allow, so there is no mismatch), and EvaluatePolicy answers allow. RunGate under enforce still sees `read`: plan mode and the read_only rung let it through. execute_governed_mcp sees `read` and runs it under MCP_DO_TOOLS=read. The gateway digest check passes because the definition did not change. So an external_write MCP tool runs in read mode and in plan mode for the rest of the segment. The plan row requires "mid-run class change fails closed". The slice's own test only covers a change that happens to be re-recorded into the view store.
review_defects.fix: At dispatch, compare the view's class and floor with the side_effect_class/approval_floor in the signed EvaluatePolicy response (or with the S3 pinned RegistryBinding), and refuse with a typed class-changed error when they differ. Or refresh the view from the S3 binding table, which is pinned at first allow, and make execute_governed_mcp read the class from there.

review_defects.where: apps/Model Plane/rust/services/execution-core/src/runtime_loop/agent.rs:3676 (retry loop) vs runtime_loop/effect.rs:65 (effect_class_of still uses name-based rung_required_for)
review_defects.scenario: With TOOL_CLASS_GATE=enforce and MCP_DO_TOOLS=read and the effect ledger on, the model calls an MCP tool declared `read`. effect_class_of classifies every mcp__ name as External (legacy rung DangerFullAccess), so the step gets one ledger reservation as an External effect. The proxy then fails with a transient transport error. tool_call_is_retryable(&run_gate, ...) now answers true, because the declared class is read, and the loop dispatches the same call up to MAX_TOOL_ATTEMPTS times under that single External reservation, finalized once. Before this slice the ledger and the retry policy used the same classifier, so an effect the ledger fences was never retried silently. That invariant is stated in the retry.rs module doc: a tool is never "risky enough to gate" and "safe enough to silently retry" at once. If the registry's `read` declaration is wrong (it comes from an untrusted annotation that someone approved), the duplicated real-world call is exactly what the ledger was meant to record and fence, and the ledger shows one action.
review_defects.fix: Classify the ledger through the same RunGate (effect_class_of should take the run's gate and use rung_required_for_with). At minimum, refuse retry whenever a ledger entry was reserved for the call as effectful.

review_defects.where: apps/Model Plane/rust/services/execution-core/src/runtime_loop/agent.rs:1072-1140 (merged_tool_defs_governed receives only req.zdr; offered_tools at :912/:927)
review_defects.scenario: A waived-route run is zero-retention and refused MCP at dispatch (mod.rs passes `zdr || waived`). Its offer still goes through the governed path. It mints an Auth Core gateway token and a capability token, calls the gateway's unstaged listing, and the gateway may run its observation write to capability-core, because the gateway decides `observe` from the service identity's posture, not the run's route. It then calls ResolveToolBindings and shows the model MCP tools that every call refuses. The slice guarantee is 'ZDR refuses MCP before any network call'. For a waived run, network calls, and possibly the durable observation write, happen on its behalf. This is disclosed as gap 3, but it is still a gap against the clause.
review_defects.fix: Pass the route's waiver into offered_tools and merged_tool_defs, and treat `zdr || waived` like zdr: skip both listings and count withheld{reason=zdr}.

review_defects.where: apps/Model Plane/rust/services/execution-core/src/permission/mod.rs:717 (take(MAX_VIEWS_PER_RUN)) with mcp_gateway.rs cap_from_raw allowing MCP_DO_TOOL_CAP up to 256
review_defects.scenario: record_run_views keeps the first 256 entries of builtin_views chained with offer.views. With MCP_DO_TOOL_CAP=256 (accepted) and about 40 built-in views, the last ~40 offered MCP tools have no view. The model is offered them, but every call fails 'not bound for this run', which is an honest refusal but a silently broken offer. Also, MAX_BINDING_NAMES truncation in resolve_run_offer drops alphabetically-late built-in names (after 'mcp__'), for example save_memory, shell and web_fetch, when the org lists more than about 200 MCP tools.
review_defects.fix: Cap MCP_DO_TOOL_CAP at MAX_VIEWS_PER_RUN minus the built-in count, or size the view store from the offer. Count the overflow as withheld{over_cap} and do not offer those tools.

review_defects.scenario: MODEL_GATEWAY_DURABLE_PLAN_GRANT=true. The user approves a plan at workspace_write on replica A, and Session Core records it. The next ordinary agentic (non-execute) run starts on A while GetThreadGrant fails: Session Core is slow past the 5 s THREAD_GRANT_TIMEOUT, a transient Unavailable, or an old session-core with no ThreadAutonomy service answers Unimplemented. durable_thread_grant turns the error into ThreadGrant::default(). resolve_autonomy_rung then returns dispatch_autonomy_rung(false,false,None) = UNSPECIFIED, which the code calls the least constrained rung a chat run can have. With the flag off, the same replica would have stated WORKSPACE_WRITE from memory. So a transient read failure silently widens the run past what the human granted. Only execute turns fail closed. Space members who are not the thread's owner always get PermissionDenied here, so they always get UNSPECIFIED, where the in-memory store gave them the thread's rung.
review_defects.fix: When the flag is on and the grant read fails, do not treat it as 'no grant' for a non-execute run. Either fail the run start with a typed retryable error, or fall back to the narrowest rung (READ_ONLY). Keep 'no grant' only for an Ok(UNSPECIFIED) answer. Add a test where the mock ThreadAutonomy errors or times out and the dispatched rung is not UNSPECIFIED.

review_defects.scenario: Flag on. A plan approval with plan_id moves the plan PROPOSED->APPROVED (transition_plan). handle_exit_plan_mode_durable then records nothing in memory and clears the local flag. Then SetRunMode fails transiently (Session Core restart, deadline, pool exhaustion). The response says persisted:false, and no grant exists anywhere: none in memory and no thread row. The plan is already APPROVED, so the approval cannot be retried because the transition is single-use. Every following execute turn gets plan_grant_unavailable, and ordinary runs get no plan block and an UNSPECIFIED rung. The handler's own comment names this exact state as the defect it was reordered to prevent ('a transient error at that point left an approved plan with no grant, and no way to retry it'). With the flag off, the in-memory grant survived on that replica.
review_defects.fix: With the flag on, make the durable write retryable before the plan is spent. Either write the grant (SetRunMode) before transition_plan, or retry SetRunMode with bounded backoff. Or, as a fallback when it fails, still record the in-memory grant so the approving replica keeps it. Add a test where SetRunMode fails with the flag on.

review_defects.scenario: The revert file's instructions are: turn MODEL_GATEWAY_DURABLE_PLAN_GRANT off on every replica, then drop the columns. But session-core's set_run_mode calls record_thread_grant whenever a grant is stated, whatever the gateway flag says. After the revert, every grant-bearing SetRunMode fails with 'column granted_rung does not exist'. That includes plan_approval with the flag off and the gRPC ExitPlanMode write-through. Because the run UPDATE is in the same transaction, it rolls back too: the run stays mode='plan' and loses its runs.metadata autonomy_rung/justification audit copy. GetThreadGrant also returns Internal. So the advertised rollback (flag off = in-memory grants, revert drops the columns) breaks the durable audit half of every approval unless session-core is rolled back at the same time. The revert file does not say this.
review_defects.fix: Gate record_thread_grant on something that survives the revert, such as a session-core-side switch or a column-existence check at boot. Otherwise, state in the revert file and the ledger rollback line that session-core must be rolled back to a build without record_thread_grant before the columns are dropped.

review_defects.scenario: Case (a): flag on. A run enters plan mode on replica A, but mark_run_plan_mode's durable SetRunMode(mode='plan') is best-effort and fails, so runs.mode stays 'execute' and only A's local flag is set. The approval reaches A: was_active = durable.unwrap_or(was_local) = false, so RUN_PLAN_MODE_EXITED, the only event carrying the granted rung, justification and plan_id, is not published. SetRunMode still writes a durable thread grant that every replica now honors. Case (b): with the flag on, the raw gRPC ExitPlanMode still uses the non-durable handle_exit_plan_mode, which keys the event on this replica's local flag. Its SetRunMode carries granted_rung, so it writes a cluster-wide durable thread grant, but if plan mode was entered on another replica no grant event is published. In both cases an authority grant becomes durable with no audit event.
review_defects.fix: In the durable path use was_active = was_in_plan_mode || was_local. Route the gRPC exit_plan_mode through handle_exit_plan_mode_durable (with the run's durable mode) when the flag is on.

review_defects.where: apps/Model Plane/rust/services/session-core/src/grpc.rs set_run_mode (~5661-5668); proto/model_plane/v1/sessions.proto SetRunModeRequest.approved_plan_id comment; migrations/0050_thread_autonomy_grant.sql header
review_defects.scenario: The new proto contract says the call is 'Refused ... for zero-retention and waived credentials: a grant is a durable record'. The migration header says 'A zero-retention or waived credential is refused before this is written'. set_run_mode only calls authorize_operation(&caller, "session:write"), and that refuses only caller.zdr(). A waived credential is a persistent token of a ZDR org with zdr=false and zdr_waiver=Some. It passes the gateway's continuation_gate (Waived is let through) and session:write, so it writes granted_rung, the free-text granted_justification and granted_plan_id onto the thread. The sibling durable run mutation record_run_context explicitly refuses `caller.zdr() || caller.zdr_waiver().is_some()`. The tests cover only zdr=true, so the stated guarantee is untested and false. WS14 S2 consumes this contract as 'refuses ZDR/waived'.
review_defects.fix: In set_run_mode, when a grant is stated, refuse `caller.zdr_waiver().is_some()` with Refusal::DURABLE_MUTATION_FORBIDDEN, as record_run_context does. Or, if waived runs are meant to keep grants, correct the proto and migration comments. Either way, add a waived-credential unit test and a DB test.

notes:
What exists. Proto: SetRunModeRequest.approved_plan_id = 6 and a new ThreadAutonomy service with GetThreadGrant, additive only. Go bindings regenerated natively. Migration 0050 is the number section 4.4 reserved and it was free; 0054 already existed, so there is no collision. It adds five nullable columns and a NOT VALID then VALIDATE CHECK on threads, and ships a revert file.

session-core: set_run_mode writes the run update and the thread grant columns in one transaction. The expiry is 24h from the DB clock. A plan id without a grant is refused. A ZDR or waived credential is refused by the existing session:write gate before anything is written. ThreadAutonomy.GetThreadGrant needs session:read plus thread-owner authorization, answers "no grant" (UNSPECIFIED) for none, lapsed or unknown label, and is registered with the other services and the health names.

Gateway, MODEL_GATEWAY_DURABLE_PLAN_GRANT default off, read once in coordinator.rs through the strict parser. session_flow::thread_grant is a bounded 5s read of GetThreadGrant (one PK read per Do-run start, no cache). With the flag on, sse.rs reads the grant once per ordinary run start. The rung and the plan id both come from that read, and the in-memory store is not consulted. A failed read counts as no grant, so an execute turn fails closed with plan_grant_unavailable. The plan claim (APPROVED to EXECUTING compare-and-swap) stays the single-use guard. In plan_approval, was_in_plan_mode = RunDetail.mode == "plan", RUN_PLAN_MODE_EXITED is published regardless of the local flag, approved_plan_id is sent, no in-memory grant is recorded, and grant_expires_at_unix is read back from session-core. With the flag off the code paths and the SetRunMode request (approved_plan_id empty) are as before.

Residual points. (1) session-core records the thread grant whenever a grant is stated, not only when approved_plan_id is set. Otherwise a rung-only approval (no plan) would not be durable. I corrected the proto comment to say so. The write is harmless when the gateway flag is off, since nothing reads the columns. (2) If SetRunMode fails with the flag on, the response says persisted:false and no grant exists anywhere (previously the in-memory grant still worked on that replica). The plan had already moved to APPROVED. I kept the existing reporting semantic and did not change it.
